faqs.question: What is the eligibility for SSC CHSL 2026?
faqs.answer: Candidates must have passed Class 12 (10+2) or equivalent from a recognised board. For DEO in C&AG and some departments, 12th with Science stream and Mathematics is required. Age must be 18-27 years as on the cut-off date (born between 1999-01-02 and 2008-01-01, approximately, for the 2026 cycle), with age relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and 10 years for PwBD as per rules.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in SSC CHSL?
faqs.answer: Yes. In Tier-1, 0.50 marks are deducted for every wrong answer. In Tier-2, 1 mark is deducted for each wrong answer in Section-I, Section-II and Module-I of Section-III (Computer Knowledge).

faqs.question: Is the Tier-2 typing/skill test mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is qualifying in nature but mandatory. DEO candidates must achieve a data entry speed of 8,000 key depressions per hour (15,000 for DEO in C&AG), while LDC/JSA candidates must type 35 words per minute in English or 30 words per minute in Hindi.

faqs.question: What is the salary for posts offered through SSC CHSL?
faqs.answer: LDC/JSA is a Pay Level-2 post (Rs 19,900 - 63,200). DEO posts are generally at Pay Level-4 (Rs 25,500 - 81,100), including DEO Grade 'A' in the Office of C&AG, while DEO posts in a few Ministries/Departments are at Level-5 (Rs 29,200 - 92,300). In-hand salary typically ranges from about Rs 26,000 to Rs 41,000 per month depending on the post and city of posting.

faqs.question: How many times is the SSC CHSL exam conducted in a year?
faqs.answer: SSC CHSL is conducted once every year. As per SSC's annual examination calendar, the CHSL 2026 notification was released around April-May 2026, with the Tier-1 exam scheduled for July-September 2026, followed by Tier-2 for shortlisted candidates.

faqs.question: Can final-year Class 12 students apply?
faqs.answer: Candidates must possess the essential 10+2 qualification on or before the cut-off date specified in the notification. Students awaiting final results can apply only if they can produce proof of passing by the stipulated date.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in SSC MTS 2026?
faqs.answer: There is no negative marking in Session I of the CBT. In Session II (General Awareness and English Language and Comprehension), 1 mark is deducted for every wrong answer.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for SSC MTS and Havaldar 2026?
faqs.answer: Candidates must have passed Matriculation (Class 10) from a recognized board. The age limit is 18-25 years for MTS and most Havaldar posts, and 18-27 years for a few MTS/Havaldar posts, with standard relaxations for OBC (3 years), SC/ST (5 years), PwBD and Ex-Servicemen categories.

faqs.question: Do all candidates have to appear for the PET/PST?
faqs.answer: No. The Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test are only for candidates who opt for the post of Havaldar in CBIC and CBN. Candidates applying only for MTS posts are selected on the basis of the Computer Based Examination alone.

faqs.question: What is the salary of an SSC MTS employee?
faqs.answer: Both MTS and Havaldar posts carry Pay Level 1 of the 7th CPC pay matrix (Rs 18,000 - 56,900 basic pay). Including DA, HRA and TA at current rates, the initial gross salary works out to roughly Rs 30,000 - 36,000 per month depending on the city of posting, with in-hand pay of about Rs 27,000 - 32,500 after deductions.

faqs.question: How is the merit list prepared if Session I has no separate cutoff marks?
faqs.answer: Session I is qualifying in nature. Final merit for MTS and Havaldar posts is prepared on the basis of normalized scores in Session II, provided the candidate has attempted Session I. Separate age-group-wise and state/UT-wise merit lists are drawn for MTS vacancies.

faqs.question: Can I apply for both MTS and Havaldar posts with one application?
faqs.answer: Yes. A single online application covers both posts; candidates indicate their preference for Havaldar (CBIC & CBN) in the form and must then qualify the PET/PST and meet the physical standards for that post.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in IBPS PO 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes. In both Prelims and Mains objective tests, 0.25 (one-fourth) of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for every wrong answer. There is no penalty for unattempted questions or for the descriptive paper.

faqs.question: Do Prelims marks count in the final IBPS PO merit list?
faqs.answer: No. The Preliminary exam is qualifying in nature. The final merit list is prepared from Mains (objective + descriptive, out of 225, normalised to 100 with 80% weight) and the Interview (100 marks, 20% weight).

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for IBPS PO 2026?
faqs.answer: A graduate degree in any discipline from a recognised university, and age between 20 and 30 years as on the cutoff date in the notification, with upper-age relaxation of 3 years for OBC (NCL), 5 years for SC/ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates.

faqs.question: How many attempts are allowed in IBPS PO?
faqs.answer: IBPS does not impose any limit on the number of attempts. Candidates can appear as many times as they wish while they satisfy the age and educational eligibility criteria.

faqs.question: Is there sectional timing in the IBPS PO Prelims?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each of the three Prelims sections (English Language, Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning Ability) has a fixed 20-minute slot, and candidates cannot switch between sections. Mains sections also have individual sectional time limits.

faqs.question: What salary does an IBPS PO get after joining?
faqs.answer: A newly recruited PO joins at Junior Management Grade Scale-I with a starting basic pay of Rs 48,480 (scale 48480-85920 under the 12th Bipartite Settlement). With DA, HRA/lease, special and learning allowances, gross monthly pay is roughly Rs 74,000-82,000, varying by posting location.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for RRB NTPC 2026?
faqs.answer: For graduate-level posts (Station Master, Goods Train Manager, Senior Clerk cum Typist, Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist, Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor, etc.) you need a university degree and age of 18-33 years; for undergraduate-level posts (Junior Clerk cum Typist, Accounts Clerk cum Typist, Trains Clerk, Commercial cum Ticket Clerk) a 10+2 pass and age of 18-30 years, as per the latest CENs (06/2025 and 07/2025). The 2024 CENs carried a one-time 3-year age extension (18-36 and 18-33) which no longer applies. Standard age relaxations apply for OBC-NCL (+3 years), SC/ST (+5 years), PwBD and Ex-Servicemen.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in RRB NTPC?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both CBT-1 and CBT-2 carry a penalty of 1/3 mark for every wrong answer. There is no negative marking in the Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT) held for Station Master and Traffic Assistant posts.

faqs.question: Is the application fee refunded?
faqs.answer: Yes, on actually appearing in CBT-1. General/OBC/EWS candidates who pay Rs. 500 get Rs. 400 refunded, while SC/ST/Female/PwBD/Ex-Servicemen/Transgender/Minorities/EBC candidates who pay Rs. 250 get the full Rs. 250 refunded, in both cases after deduction of applicable bank charges.

faqs.question: Are marks normalized across shifts?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since CBT-1 and CBT-2 are conducted in multiple shifts with different question papers, RRBs use percentile-based normalization of marks, and shortlisting/cutoffs are computed on normalized scores.

faqs.question: Can I apply to more than one RRB?
faqs.answer: No. A candidate can apply to only one RRB in a given CEN, and only one application per candidate is allowed. Submitting multiple applications leads to rejection and possible debarment.

faqs.question: How many candidates are shortlisted for CBT-2?
faqs.answer: Candidates equal to about 15 times the number of vacancies (community-wise) for each pay level are shortlisted from CBT-1 for CBT-2, based on merit in normalized CBT-1 marks, as per recent CENs (RRBs reserve the right to increase or decrease this ratio). CBT-1 is only a screening test; final merit is based on CBT-2 (plus CBAT/typing test where applicable).

faqs.question: What is the typing speed requirement for typist posts?
faqs.answer: For posts like Senior Clerk cum Typist, Junior Accounts Assistant cum Typist and Junior Clerk cum Typist, candidates must type 30 words per minute in English or 25 words per minute in Hindi on a computer without editing tools/spell-check. The typing test is qualifying in nature.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in MPPSC State Service Prelims 2026?
faqs.answer: No. MPPSC does not apply negative marking in the State Service Preliminary Examination. Both Paper I (General Studies) and Paper II (General Aptitude Test) carry 200 marks each with no penalty for wrong answers. Paper II is qualifying in nature with a minimum of 40% marks required.

faqs.question: How many attempts are allowed in the MPPSC State Service Exam?
faqs.answer: MPPSC does not prescribe a fixed number of attempts. Candidates can appear as many times as they wish within the eligible age limit, which is generally 21 to 40 years for MP domicile candidates (with relaxations for reserved categories and government servants as per state rules) and 21 to 28 years for other-state candidates for uniformed posts like DSP.

faqs.question: Which posts are filled through the MPPSC State Service Examination?
faqs.answer: The State Service Examination recruits for State Civil Services posts such as Deputy Collector, Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP), Commercial Tax Officer, District Registrar, Cooperative Inspector, Naib Tahsildar and various other Class II and Class III posts of the Madhya Pradesh government.

faqs.question: What is the medium of the MPPSC Mains examination?
faqs.answer: Candidates may write the Mains papers in Hindi or English, except the General Hindi paper and the Hindi Essay paper, which must be answered in Hindi. Question papers are set bilingually in Hindi and English.

faqs.question: Do Prelims marks count in the final merit list?
faqs.answer: No. The Preliminary examination is only a screening stage. Final merit is prepared out of 1575 marks, comprising the six Mains papers (1400 marks) and the Interview/Personality Test (175 marks).

faqs.question: Can candidates from outside Madhya Pradesh apply for MPPSC SSE 2026?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates from other states can apply, but they are treated as unreserved category regardless of their home-state category, pay the full application fee of Rs 500, and are not eligible for MP-specific age and fee relaxations.

faqs.q: How many attempts are allowed in UPPSC PCS?
faqs.a: UPPSC does not limit the number of attempts. You can appear as many times as you like between the ages of 21 and 40 (upper age relaxable by 5 years for SC/ST/OBC candidates domiciled in Uttar Pradesh).

faqs.q: Is the CSAT (GS Paper II) counted for the Prelims merit list?
faqs.a: No. GS Paper II (CSAT) is only qualifying - you need at least 33% in it. The Prelims cutoff and shortlisting for Mains are decided solely on GS Paper I marks.

faqs.q: Is there negative marking in UPPSC PCS Prelims?
faqs.a: Yes. One-third (1/3) of the marks assigned to a question is deducted for every wrong answer in both Prelims papers. There is no negative marking in the descriptive Mains papers.

faqs.q: Can candidates from outside Uttar Pradesh apply?
faqs.a: Yes, candidates from any state can apply. However, the benefit of reservation (SC/ST/OBC/EWS quotas, and horizontal reservation for women and PwBD) and the category fee concessions is limited to candidates domiciled in Uttar Pradesh; all others are treated as unreserved.

faqs.q: Does UPPSC PCS still have optional subjects in Mains?
faqs.a: No. Since the 2022 reform, optional subjects have been removed from the Mains. The Mains now has 8 compulsory papers - General Hindi (150), Essay (150) and six General Studies papers of 200 marks each, of which GS-V and GS-VI are Uttar Pradesh specific - totalling 1500 marks, plus a 100-mark interview.

faqs.q: What posts are offered through UPPSC PCS 2026?
faqs.a: Top posts include Deputy Collector (SDM) and Deputy Superintendent of Police (both Pay Level 10, Rs 56,100 - 1,77,500), along with Block Development Officer, Assistant Regional Transport Officer, District Commandant Home Guards, Treasury Officer and other Group A and B posts of the UP government. Around 500 vacancies have been advertised for the 2026 cycle, and UPPSC has historically increased the count during the recruitment (2024: 220 to 947; 2025: 200 to 920).

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in the BPSC CCE Prelims?
faqs.answer: No. BPSC had proposed 1/4 negative marking for the 68th CCE but withdrew it, and the Prelims (150 questions, 150 marks) currently has no negative marking. The qualifying Optional MCQ paper in Mains also has no negative marking.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for BPSC CCE 2026?
faqs.answer: A bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognized university. Minimum age is 20/21/22 years depending on the post (22 for DSP), and maximum age is 37 years for unreserved male candidates, 40 for female/BC/EBC and 42 for SC/ST, reckoned as on 1 August 2026.

faqs.question: How is the final merit list prepared?
faqs.answer: Final merit is based on 1020 marks: Mains written papers counted for merit (GS Paper I 300 + GS Paper II 300 + Essay 300 = 900) plus the Interview of 120 marks. Prelims, General Hindi and the Optional paper are qualifying only.

faqs.question: How many attempts are allowed in BPSC CCE?
faqs.answer: BPSC does not impose a fixed attempt limit; candidates can appear as many times as they remain within the age limit for their category.

faqs.question: Can candidates from outside Bihar apply?
faqs.answer: Yes, candidates from any state can apply, but they are treated as unreserved (general) category regardless of their caste category, and reservation plus fee concessions apply only to Bihar domicile candidates.

faqs.question: In which language is the exam conducted?
faqs.answer: Question papers are bilingual (Hindi and English). Mains answers can be written in Hindi, English or Urdu, while the General Hindi paper must be attempted in Hindi and is qualifying with 30% minimum marks.

faqs.question: What is the eligibility for RPSC RAS 2026?
faqs.answer: A Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a UGC-recognised university, and age between 21 and 40 years as on 1 January 2027. Final-year graduation students can appear in Prelims but must furnish proof of graduation before the Mains. Age relaxation applies for reserved categories of Rajasthan as per state rules.

faqs.question: Is there negative marking in the RAS Prelims?
faqs.answer: Yes. One-third (1/3) of a mark is deducted for every wrong answer in the 150-question, 200-mark Prelims paper. RPSC also uses a fifth option for 'not attempted'; leaving more than 10% of questions without marking any of the five options can lead to disqualification, so fill the fifth bubble for questions you skip.

faqs.question: Do Prelims marks count in the final merit list?
faqs.answer: No. The Prelims is only a screening test. The final merit is prepared out of 900 marks — 800 from the four Mains papers (200 each) plus 100 from the interview.

faqs.question: How many attempts are allowed in RPSC RAS?
faqs.answer: There is no limit on the number of attempts. Candidates can appear as many times as they wish while they remain within the 21-40 age band (with applicable category relaxations).

faqs.question: What is the application fee for RAS 2026?
faqs.answer: Under Rajasthan's One Time Registration system, General and Creamy-Layer OBC/MBC candidates pay Rs 600, while OBC-NCL/MBC-NCL, EWS, SC, ST, PwBD and candidates with annual family income below Rs 2.5 lakh pay Rs 400. This OTR fee is paid once and covers all future RPSC applications.

faqs.question: What is the salary of an RAS officer?
faqs.answer: RAS and other State Services posts start at Rajasthan Pay Matrix Level L-14 with a basic pay of Rs 56,100 (Grade Pay 5400 equivalent), which works out to roughly Rs 72,000-85,000 in hand per month with allowances. Subordinate Services posts such as Tehsildar start at lower pay levels (Grade Pay 4200-4800 equivalent).

faqs.question: In which language is the RAS exam conducted?
faqs.answer: Question papers for Prelims and the General Studies Mains papers are bilingual (Hindi and English). Paper IV of Mains specifically tests General Hindi (120 marks) and General English (80 marks).
